parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a national framework with universal-exposure measures enforced at every entry: passport markers restricted to birth sex, X markers blocked, a visa case-note tag and a 'reasonable doubt on sex' refusal instruction with a lifetime fraud ground, and documented confiscation/stranding of travellers. Outed visitors also face state facility bans in many states, criminal trespass in four, and documented birth-sex custody harm, immigration-custody abuse and care cuts. The state/province adds a minors' care ban (affecting travelling families), a Medicaid/prison care bar, and no gender-identity non-discrimination, partially offset by a gender-identity hate-crime statute. No execution or presentation criminalisation; consequences are harassment, stranding, fraud findings, wrong-sex custody and care denial — heavy but below the 0.35 anchors' severity, above the 0.45 anchors' single facility rule. 0.40.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal-exposure: passports only as M/F per birth sex, X markers ceased, 'reasonable doubt on sex' refusal and fraud ground, case-note tag; documented passport confiscation and stranding of travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties union suit challenging the passport policy; existing X passports valid until expiration; foreign governments' travel advisories.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can trigger investigation and permanent fraud ineligibility; national rules apply to every visitor.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented birth-sex custody harm, immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse; passport confiscation before travel; state prison care cut-off with no taper plan.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; the earlier prison LGBTQ executive order was rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry screening can escalate into investigation and detention; state/province custody placement for a visitor is not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in many states, criminal trespass in four, arrest under a bathroom law (handcuffed, men's ward custody); the national framework bars congruent facilities in national facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented; the state/province's own facility ban is not documented (no local arrest rule).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State rules apply to visitors regardless of home documents; exposure varies by itinerary but is universal within restricted states.

care_services.exposure: State/province bans minors' hormones/blockers/surgery (a travelling minor cannot continue care); Medicaid bar for all ages; prison care cut-off; licence revocation and 15-year patient lawsuits chill providers.
care_services.protection: Adults already in treatment may continue; two sanctuary cities; two comparable laws elsewhere blocked by national courts.
care_services.interaction: Medicaid exclusion applies to visitors using public coverage; a travelling-with-minor family faces the full ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State framing of trans people as deceptive ('mutilation' language, 'radical gender ideology' in counterterrorism strategy); statewide anti-trans tipline for reporting 'gender transition intervention'; 66% public support for birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment discrimination protection and gender-identity hate-crime statute remain; the state/province's hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing raises outing probability via tipline and state enforcement culture.

minors_guardians.exposure: State/province SAFE Act blocks all minors' care; national care ban for minors and school-prosecution order; national subpoena of hospital records of patients under 19.
minors_guardians.protection: Grandfathering for those already in treatment; ban sunsets 2027 but initiative seeks permanence; litigation upheld.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor cannot continue care; the state/province's own school-prosecution exposure is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented; no dated incident of violence against a trans person in the state/province with an outcome.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute covers gender identity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The civil-liberties union's passport suit, the state/province's care ban, and the state/province custody placement rule are unresolved; the state/province's own facility ban is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Twenty-two state/provinces plus the capital district protect gender identity; this state/province does not.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal-aid organisation maintains an FAQ; the state/province's own court placement rule is not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A features a single universal-exposure rule (birth-sex facility admission) with no remedy; the national regime here reaches further (document restriction, visa fraud ground, custody harms) but severity is moderate (no execution, no presentation criminalisation), so the jurisdiction sits slightly above 0.35-A's severity.

0.45-A is a single birth-sex facility rule plus a prosecuted assault; the national regime here is a broader universal-exposure measure (passport restriction plus entry screening) and the state/province adds a care ban for minors, so it sits below 0.45-A despite the hate-crime statute.

0.55-B has no universal-exposure rule and recourse working in some districts; the national regime here imposes a universal-exposure document rule with no remedy, which is a heavier tier-1 exposure, so the jurisdiction sits materially below 0.55-B.

The state/province adds a minors' care ban (affecting travelling families), a Medicaid/prison care bar, and no gender-identity non-discrimination, partially offset by a gender-identity hate-crime statute. No execution or presentation criminalisation; consequences are harassment, stranding, fraud findings, wrong-sex custody and care denial — heavy but below the 0.35 anchors' severity, above the 0.45 anchors' single facility rule. 0.40.
